subtype: Approach: checklist of emergency numbers on the fridge [Action]
passage: Saturday. Amma and Papa wrote a card today: fire brigade, ambulance, and Salma Aunty next door. They stuck it on the fridge with the mango magnet. Then Papa said, "Now you call. Pretend." I held the old phone, pressed nothing, and said, "Hello, there is a fire at 14 Lake View Colony, second floor." The first time my voice went squeaky. The second time it was normal. The third time Amma timed me and I said the whole thing slowly, like a news reader. I like knowing the card is there. 🙂 - Madhuri

qa.q: Where did the family stick the card?
qa.a: They stuck it on the fridge.

qa.q: How did Madhuri feel about the card at the end of the day?
qa.a: Reassured, since Madhuri likes knowing the card is there.

qa.q: What could the family do to make the practice more realistic, and why?
qa.a: A family member could play the operator and ask questions, so Madhuri practises answering while a little nervous.

qa.q: How might Salma Aunty feel about being on the card?
qa.a: Salma Aunty is probably trusted and glad to help, as a neighbour who can arrive quickly.

grounding: A family puts emergency numbers on a card near the door and the child practises calling and giving the address.
